name: Nadifloxacin

lead: Nadifloxacin is a 1% antibiotic cream for acne and skin infections, available in Japan, some European and Asian countries.
Small studies reportedly show lesion reductions comparable to clindamycin combinations, but evidence in the sources is limited.

paras: It inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase, killing or stopping acne-related bacteria such as Cutibacterium acnes, and may have anti-inflammatory effects.
Mostly local burning, itching, dryness. Wikipedia notes concern that topical quinolones could promote resistance. Not approved in the US.

lead: Nadifloxacin is a topical fluoroquinolone antibiotic used mainly for acne vulgaris and, secondarily, for bacterial skin infections. [1][2] It inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase. [2]

It is marketed as a 1% cream in Japan, parts of Europe and some Asian countries, and is not approved in the United States. [1][2] Wikipedia notes concern that topical quinolone use could promote quinolone resistance. [2]
infobox: Otsuka (code OPC-7251); Japan approval 1993 per Grokipedia [1]
Approved in Japan and some other countries; not in the US [1][2]

paras: Nadifloxacin is used for mild to moderate acne and for pyodermas such as impetigo and folliculitis. [1][2] Grokipedia says it is often used with benzoyl peroxide or adapalene. [1]
Adverse reactions are mostly local: burning, itching (most common), contact dermatitis, dryness and irritation. [2]

It inhibits DNA gyrase, halting bacterial replication, and may have sebostatic and anti-inflammatory effects. [2] In vitro it is active against Cutibacterium acnes, Staphylococcus epidermidis and MRSA. [2] After a single large application of 1% cream, peak plasma level was 107 ng/mL with a half-life of 19.4 hours. [2]
It is a racemic fluoroquinolone, formula C19H21FN2O4, molar mass about 360.4 g/mol. [2]

Wikipedia cites a 2013 Japanese study in which nadifloxacin 1% combined with adapalene 0.1% gel improved inflammatory papulopustular lesions more than adapalene alone. [2] Grokipedia (AI-generated, less reliable) reports trials comparing nadifloxacin with benzoyl peroxide combinations to clindamycin combinations with similar lesion reductions, and Korean and Indian studies. [1] A registered phase 4 trial comparing nadifloxacin plus tretinoin with clindamycin plus tretinoin for mild-to-moderate acne is recruiting. [3]
